inlines.latex: \begin{aligned}|ABX|&=2.836\text{ cm}^2\\|BCY|=|ADZ|&=2.831\text{ cm}^2\\|BXY|=|AXZ|&=3.488\text{ cm}^2\\|CYZD|&=6.301\text{ cm}^2\\|ABCD|&=2.000\text{ cm}^2\\|XYZ|&=1.299\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}

inlines.text: Find perpendicular face heights using Pythagoras, then use triangle and trapezium area formulas.

answer.worked:
Let $a=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ and $b=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$. The offsets from each end-plane centre are $(\pm a,\pm a)$ for the square and $X=(0,1)$, $Y=(-b,-\frac12)$, $Z=(b,-\frac12)$ for the triangle. Lengths are in centimetres.

The square side is $2a=\sqrt2$ and the equilateral triangle side is $2b=\sqrt3$.

Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$. The height from $X$ to $AB$ is $XM$, since the horizontal offset of $X$ is zero. By Pythagoras,
$$\begin{align*}XM^2&=4^2+(1-a)^2\\XM&=\sqrt{16+(1-a)^2}\\|ABX|&=\frac12(2a)\sqrt{16+(1-a)^2}\\|ABX|&\approx2.836\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$

For $BCY$, the perpendicular from $Y$ meets $BC$ at vertical offset $-\frac12$. Its height $h_1$ combines the centre separation and horizontal offset $b-a$:
$$\begin{align*}h_1^2&=4^2+(b-a)^2\\|BCY|=|ADZ|&=\frac12(2a)\sqrt{16+(b-a)^2}\\|BCY|=|ADZ|&\approx2.831\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$

To find the height of $BXY$, project $B$ perpendicularly onto the triangle's end plane at $B'$. In that plane, the line $XY$ makes $60^\circ$ with the horizontal. The perpendicular distance $d$ from $B'$ to $XY$ is
$$\begin{align*}d&=a\sin60^\circ+a\cos60^\circ-\frac12\\d&=a\left(b+\frac12\right)-\frac12.\end{align*}$$
The perpendicular height $h_2$ of $BXY$ follows by Pythagoras:
$$\begin{align*}h_2^2&=4^2+d^2\\|BXY|=|AXZ|&=\frac12(2b)\sqrt{16+\left[a\left(b+\frac12\right)-\frac12\right]^2}\\|BXY|=|AXZ|&\approx3.488\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$

The parallel sides of trapezium $CYZD$ are $CD=2a$ and $YZ=2b$. Its perpendicular height $h_3$ combines the centre separation and vertical offset $a-\frac12$:
$$\begin{align*}h_3^2&=4^2+\left(a-\frac12\right)^2\\|CYZD|&=\frac12(2a+2b)\sqrt{16+\left(a-\frac12\right)^2}\\|CYZD|&\approx6.301\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$

For the two end faces,
$$\begin{align*}|ABCD|&=(\sqrt2)^2\\|ABCD|&=2.000\text{ cm}^2\\|XYZ|&=\frac12(\sqrt3)\left(1+\frac12\right)\\|XYZ|&=\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}\\|XYZ|&\approx1.299\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
